exposure: Fetal open surgery for occipital encephalocele
outcome: Premature Cesarean section due to uterine wall thinning
Newborn discharged from neonatal intensive care unit in good condition
Newborn discharged from hospital in good condition
cohort: A single fetus diagnosed with occipital encephalocele underwent fetal open surgery in a Brazilian Public Health Service.
finding: The first fetal open surgery for occipital encephalocele in Brazil successfully resulted in a newborn discharged in good condition, though a premature Cesarean section was necessitated by maternal complications.
mod_finding: A premature Cesarean section was indicated at 34 + 4 weeks due to significant thinning of the myometrial wall with risk of uterine rupture, suggesting a maternal risk associated with the fetal surgery.
gest_age: Fetal surgery performed at 27 + 2 weeks; delivery occurred at 34 + 4 weeks.
